evan: Heads-up — ran an overnight GPU capability sweep on staging and hit a baffling BF16->FP32 fallback on some A100 hosts around seqlen 1k-2k. Dumped probe output and microbench results.

jia: Is this the kv-cache seqlen gating change from last week?

ev an: Yep, batching heuristics + kv-cache hot-prefix. The selector initially picks the bf16-tc kernel but at runtime we observe a fallback to the generic fp32 path for certain seqlen buckets. p95 jumps ~28%.

omar: Driver regression possibility? Which driver/build on the nodes?

ev an: These hosts are on driver 525.85. Command I used: `./tools/gpu_probe.sh --json > /tmp/probe-a100-2103.json`. Snippet: 

```
sm: 8.0
driver: 525.85
tensor_cores: true
supports_bf16_tensorcore: true
kernel_candidates: [bf16_tc, bf16_slow, fp32_generic]
selector_initial: bf16_tc
runtime_fallback: fp32_generic (trigger at seq_len=1536)
```

perf-bot: microbench results (automated): model=gpt-large, batch=1
- bf16_tc @ seq=1536: 12.1 tok/ms
- fp32_generic @ seq=1536: 8.7 tok/ms
(delta ~ -28% throughput when fallback happens)

rachel: Could prefix merging / kv-cache layout shift the memory layout so the tc kernel fails its memory-layout check and falls back?

jia: Our gating logic currently: `if sm>=80 && driver>=525 then consider_tc` and a seqlen bucket rule `<1024 fastpath`. But we also rely on `max_concurrent_heads` that some firmware reports incorrectly which can steer us away from the tc kernel.

omar: Suggest adding a derived capability flag like `hw.bf16_tc_stable` computed by a tiny microprobe that runs the candidate tc kernel on a tiny microbatch and checks correctness & perf. If it passes, mark node stable for tc.

ev an: I can prototype an opt-in: `REDWOOD_EXPERIMENTAL_FORCE_TC=true` to force prefer tc on Dedicated canaries. Quick runtime patch: `if (cap.has_bf16_tc && microbench_ok) choose('bf16_tc');`

rachel: Also add structured logging for fallback reasons: `fallback_reason={memory_layout_mismatch|driver_quirk|seqlen_gate|perf_regression}` so we can correlate in Console traces.

ev an: Agree — will add `fallback_reason` into token-level traces and rollout as a low-overhead enum.

jia: Can someone run the probe with rechecks on affected hosts: `python -m tools.probes.gpu --recheck --samples 3` and drop the outputs in #eng-runtime? I'll write a parser to aggregate the `microbench_ok` and compute a per-host stability score.

ev an: Done — uploaded tarball to S3: s3://redwood-staging/probes/210345_a100_fallbacks.tar.gz. cc @jia

omar: :thumbsup: I'll kick off a dedicated microbench sweep (vary seq_len 512/1024/1536/2048, batch 1-4) and post summarized numbers. If we confirm a consistent perf cliff we can flip the canary flag.

infra-bot: deploy canary started: `canary/dedicated-force-tc-5nodes` (ids: dc-a100-21..25)

rachel: One more thing — capture the kernel selector inputs (head count, kv-shard-layout, workspace_bytes) in the probe output. Without those we can't reproduce the memory-layout mismatch.

ev an: Will add those fields to the probe JSON and re-run. Plan: 1) instrument selector to emit fallback_reason, 2) add microprobe-derived `hw.bf16_tc_stable`, 3) run canary with `FORCE_TC` on 5 nodes, 4) collect perf & traces and decide.

jia: Perfect. If we see driver-specific failures we can gate on `driver >= 535` for the fp8/bf16 fastpath in the next rollout.

ev an: Opening a follow-up issue with logs and steps to reproduce. Will post link when ready.

omar: I'll follow up with the microbench numbers in this thread once complete.

(Short thread — keeping it focused; thanks everyone)
